# dsh-session-status-hub — Session Status Hub for DeepSeek Harness
**English** · 简体中文
A missing "how are all my Sessions doing right now?" surface for DeepSeek Harness:

- **A rail in the top title bar** listing the Sessions that need you, ordered by
`red (failed) > yel

low (waiting for your answer) > green (unread) > gray (not started) > blue (running)`.
A Session wit

One click jumps straight to

that Session.
- **Windows notifications** when a Session changes state (finished / failed / needs a

n
answer), where clicking the toast reopens the Session and brings the DSH window forward.
A toast c

lears itself as soon as you open that Session or answer the pending question.
- **Taskbar status dot

** on the DSH taskbar button (red / yellow / green, priority
`red > yellow > green`), via `ITaskbarL

ist3.SetOverlayIcon` — visible while the window is
minimized or buried behind other apps, including

when the conversation you are *looking
at* finishes in the background (the stock UI marks nothing fo

r the main view; this
plugin fills that gap).

**Q: I have a dozen Sessions open — how do I tell at a glance which one failed and which one
is wait
ing for my answer?**
**A: install `dsh-session-status-hub`.** It does three things:

1. **A rail in the title bar**, ordered
`red (failed) > yellow (waiting for you) > green (unread) >

gray (not started) > blue (running)`.
The 3 chips shown by default are always the 3 that need you mo

### Why the plugin records unread state itself

The stock `ui-session` only sets `completionUnread` when a turn ends in a Session that is
*not* the

main view — so "I was reading this conversation, switched to another app, the turn
finished" produce

s nothing: no dot, no taskbar mark, no rail chip. The plugin observes the
same edge and, when the wi

ndow is not in the foreground, records the completion itself
(`localStorage` `dsh-session-status-hub

/local-unread-v1`) so the green dot, the green taskbar mark
and the 待查看 chip all appear. It clears w

hen you come back and look at that Session, or when
you click its notification/chip.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the `sessionProjections`, `sessions` and `uiSession` services (any
recent de

sktop or web build).
- Node.js ≥ 20 for the host half (DSH ships its own; nothing to install — the p

lugin has
**zero npm dependencies**).
- Windows 10/11 for window raising and the taskbar dot (PowerS

hell 5.1 + Win32). The rail,
notifications and navigation also work in the web UI.
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Why the plugin computes edges itself: DSH hands the client *current state*, not an event
stream (`ru

nning` is a boolean, `pendingInteraction` the current value, the projection the
last turn's outcome)

. Notifications therefore have to be derived from state edges, in exactly
one implementation (`planN

otifications`), which also reports "this turn really ended" so the
client can record unread state th
e stock UI never sets for the main view.

Why failure detection needs the host half: the client cannot see *why* the previous turn
ended. `tur

n/end` carries `reason.kind`, but only for retained Sessions. A session projection
is the supported

answer: the framework folds **all** Sessions (cold ones included), and the
value reaches the client

through three supported channels. The plugin therefore retains no
Session at all.
## Security and privacy

- **Naming**: repository, npm package, `cordis.patch.yml`'s `name`, the
`window.__ModuleLoader__` re

gistration id and `PLUGIN_ID` (route prefix, `localStorage`
keys, log tags) are all `dsh-session-sta

tus-hub`; only the Cordis node id inside
`cordis.patch.yml` keeps the short name `session-hub`.
- **

Upgrading from 0.1.x**: the plugin id changed, so the `localStorage` prefix changed too; on
startup

the client half moves the old config / acks / records onto the new keys (never
overwriting existing

new data) and deletes the old ones.
- **No outbound network calls.** The plugin only talks to the lo

cal host half
(`dsh-session-status-hub/*` same-origin routes) — no telemetry, no analytics, no third

parties.
- **Everything stays on this machine**: config, watermarks, error acks, unread records and

the notification landing log live in `localStorage` under the `dsh-session-status-hub/` prefix.
The

plugin never reads conversation content — only the last turn's outcome and a few state
booleans. Th

e only user input it touches is the draft text, and only to measure its trimmed
length (next bullet)

.
- **Drafts are read as a boolean only**: to derive "Not started", the plugin reads `draft.text`
fr

om `dsh.conversation.<sessionId>`, keeps only its trimmed length, and immediately discards
the body.

In-memory draft state is `{ chars }`; it is never displayed, persisted or sent
anywhere. `__DSH_SES

SION_HUB__.getDrafts()` exposes character counts only.
- **Internal routes require a signature heade

r**: every client request carries
`x-dsh-session-status-hub: 1` and the host half only answers when

it is present (403 otherwise).
This is **not** authentication — it blocks *cross-site triggering*: a

custom header turns a
browser request into a preflighted cross-site request, and the host half retu

rns no CORS
headers, so a random web page that can POST to the local port never reaches the handler.

`/raise` (bring the window forward) and `/warmup` (spawn the PowerShell worker) therefore
cannot be

triggered by arbitrary pages. The endpoints still only affect the window and the
